title: AES recommended practice for professional audio interconnections — Conservation of the polarity of audio signals
working_group: SC-05-05 (Working Group on Grounding and EMC Practices)
abstract: This document standardizes the polarity of the signals at the various interface points between different items of equipment, in particular from the acoustical, electrical, mechanical, digital, and magnetic aspects. Each item of equipment complies separately with the polarity requirements for the input and output signals.
scope: Applies to professional audio equipment, sound reinforcement systems, studio recording, and broadcast facilities. Establishes requirements to preserve absolute signal polarity from sound pressure in air, through transducers, mixing consoles, processors, recording media, and back to acoustic sound waves radiated by loudspeakers.
normative_references: AES14: Application of connectors, part 1, XLR-type polarity and gender
IEC 60268-2: Sound system equipment - Part 2: Explanation of general terms and calculation methods
IEC 60268-12: Application of connectors for broadcast and similar use
IEC 60094-1: Magnetic tape sound recording and reproducing systems

key_definitions.positive_polarity: An instantaneous positive audio signal corresponding to positive acoustic sound pressure.
key_definitions.positive_sound_pressure: A portion of the sound wave where acoustic pressure exceeds atmospheric pressure.
key_definitions.in_phase: Signals whose waveforms maintain identical sign and time alignment across channels.

polarity_specifications.microphones: Positive sound pressure incident upon the front of a microphone diaphragm produces a positive electrical voltage on XLR Pin 2 relative to Pin 3.
polarity_specifications.loudspeakers: Positive electrical voltage applied to the designated '+' or non-black terminal causes the speaker diaphragm/cone to move outwardly toward the listener, creating positive acoustic sound pressure.
polarity_specifications.amplifiers: A positive input signal produces a non-inverted positive output signal. In bridged mono mode, the lower numbered channel retains input polarity, while the higher numbered channel is inverted.
polarity_specifications.xlr_connectors: Pin 2 is positive polarity relative to Pin 3 (complying with AES14).
polarity_specifications.concentric_connectors: Balanced: Tip positive relative to Ring. Unbalanced: Tip positive relative to Sleeve.
polarity_specifications.magnetic_tape: Magnetization of tape in the direction of tape travel corresponds to positive audio signal.
polarity_specifications.digital_systems: Positive acoustic sound pressure peak is represented by positive numerical values in two's complement linear PCM encoding.

verification_methods.test_waveform: Asymmetric half-wave rectified sawtooth pulse (400 μs ramp, 100 μs fall, 500 μs baseline) used to verify reproducing and recording channel polarity without ambiguity.

relevance_to_balanced_audio: Establishes Rule 5 of balanced audio: Absolute polarity must be conserved end-to-end. Without strict adherence to AES26, multi-microphone acoustic summing, stereo imaging, and subwoofer phase alignment suffer severe acoustic cancellation.
